Volunteer

Volunteer

19–27 November 2026
Be part of the team that brings the festival to life.

Doha Film Festival (DFF) returns this November, bringing a dynamic slate of films from Qatar, the region and around the world to audiences in Doha, alongside talks, community events and special programmes. None of it happens without our volunteers, and we would love for you to be one of them.

Why Volunteer?

Who Can Apply?

Shortly after receiving your application, our Volunteer Team will invite candidates to a friendly Meet and Greet session. Selected volunteers will then be notified of their role, department, and invited to a Volunteer Orientation ahead of the festival.

For any questions, please reach out to us at volunteer@dohafilm.com

We look forward to welcoming you to the DFF Volunteer Team!

Join us from 1–3 October 2026, as Geekend brings Qatar’s creative communities together once more at the Geekdom Building on Lusail Boulevard for three days of art games, stories, and everything in between.

This edition shines its spotlight on artists, with a floor full of art-led activities and competitions alongside all the things you know and love, such as…

  • The Geekend Market, packed with original art, crafts, and collectables from local creators
  • A brand-new edition of our fan-favourite Escape Room
  • Board games, side quests, workshops, and community art walls
  • Trivia, karaoke, and live moments on the Geekend stage

Our floor activities run throughout opening hours, so whether you arrive at 3:00 PM sharp or drop in after dinner, there’s always something to play, make, watch, or win!

Casual player or completionist, this is your invitation to geek out among your peers!

Dates: 1–3 October 2026
Time: 3:00 PM – 11:00 PM daily
Location: Geekdom Building, Lusail Boulevard
Day Pass: QAR 25 (tickets on sale soon)

Our full line-up is loading…
Stay tuned to this space.

The Ajyal Jury experience invites young people aged 16 to 25 to be at the heart of the conversation. Watch international cinema, learn directly from filmmakers, and decide some of Doha Film Festival’s prestigious awards.

Becoming an Ajyal Juror is your chance to connect with new cultures, build lasting friendships, and play a vital role in recognising films that speak to your generation. 

This unique programme goes beyond film viewing. It is your invitation to discover how cinema creates space for dialogue, reflection, and connection.

Eligibility: Ages 16–25
Location: Katara Cultural Village.
Registration Fee: QR 500

  • Early Bird Fee: QR 250 (available from 13 September to 3 October 2026)
  • Discounted Fee for Siblings: QR 350 (with code applied at registration)

Registration opens on 13 September and closes on 8 November 2026.

Please note: Participants under 18 will require parental or guardian consent.

Ajyal Film Club: Festival Edition

    FAQ

Ajyal Film Club: Festival Edition

    FAQ

Share ideas and discover how stories connect us all in this special three-day experience.

For younger film fans, the Ajyal Film Club: Festival Edition is a newly expanded three-day experience designed specifically for young people aged 8 to 15. Through carefully curated films, creative activities, and meaningful conversations, participants develop new perspectives and a deeper understanding of the world around us.

The Ajyal Film Club encourages curiosity, empathy, and self-expression, helping young audiences see film as both entertainment and a tool for dialogue and discovery. The experience is grouped into two separate streams by age:

  • Mohaq (Ages 8–11): 20, 21 & 22 November
  • Hilal (Ages 12–15): 23, 24 & 25 November

Eligibility: Ages 8–15
Location: Katara Cultural Village. 
Dates: 20–25 November 2026 (three days per age group)
Registration Fee: QR 150

Registration opens on 13 September and closes on 8 November 2026.

Please note: Participants under 18 will require parental or guardian consent.

items.content_html:
Our development team offers one-to-one consultations for filmmakers based in Qatar, providing tailored creative support across all stages of a project’s evolution.

Whether you are shaping an initial idea, refining a script, or preparing a project for production, our sessions are designed to help you strengthen your story, deepen your vision, and identify your next creative steps.

We work exclusively with filmmakers who have been living in Qatar for at least one year.

During the consultation, our team engages directly with your material—be it a concept note, a script draft, or a developed pitch. Based on your needs, we provide feedback on narrative structure, character development, visual storytelling, and thematic clarity.

Our goal is to empower storytellers with the insight and support needed to move forward with purpose and confidence.

Interested in a consultation?

Please email development@dohafilm.com with:

  • A brief overview of your project
  • Its current stage of development
  • Areas where you would like support
  • A copy of your QID

We look forward to hearing from you soon!

Doha Film Institute (DFI) celebrates another major milestone with eight Institute-supported films selected for the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

12th Edition to Offer Mentorship Support to 49 Projects from 39 Countries

Palestine 36 presents a living archive of a defining chapter in history, said director Annemarie Jacir, following a special private screening of the movie at Doha Film Festival.

Arab film industry must build its own model, one that is rooted in cultural authenticity that speaks to regional audiences and is powered by co-productions, said experts at a panel discussion at Doha Film Festival 2025.

Geekend Market

Where Qatar’s creators set up shop.

The Geekend Market is where Qatar’s creators share their original art, handmade crafts, collectables, and merchandise you won’t find in any shop, sold by the people who made them to the people who get it.

This year, artists take centre stage at Geekend, so if you’ve ever wanted to turn your passion project into a stall with a queue, this is your side quest made main event.

Claim your seat at the table

Applications are now open for artists, vendors, and exhibitors:

  • Artist table: QAR 450
  • Vendor table: QAR 900 

Spaces are strictly limited and allocated on review, so early applications are strongly encouraged, applications must adhere to the following criteria:

PDF file with clear photos of each item and clear pricing and quantities.

Apply now!

Applications close: 01 September 2026

Visiting rather than selling? 

Come treat yourself, meet the makers, and support local talent. Our Geekend Market runs throughout the event, 1–3 October 2026.

Cinema by the Sea

A Made in Qatar Showcase from Doha Film Institute

This Ramadan, Doha Film Institute brings people together through cinema at the Throwback Food Festival. Set against the serene backdrop of Old Doha Port, our open-air screenings create a family-friendly space to connect, reflect, and enjoy a shared cultural moment by the sea.

Join us each night from Thursday, 26 February to Saturday, 28 February at 8.30 PM for a curated selection of Made in Qatar short films celebrating our traditions, stories, and local filmmaking community.

26 – 28 Feb, 8:30 PM
Old Doha Port

  • Sh'hab (2018) by Amal Al-Muftah

  • Under the Lemon Tree (2020) by Noor Al-Assead
  • Al Tabbab (2020) by Khalifa al Mana
  • Civilization of Equality (2023) by Ibrahim Albuainain
  • Makh'bz (2015) by Aisha Al Muhannadi

  • Hope (2020) by Abdulla Al Janahi
